Adam loves sports, especially football. Every weekend,

ball and wears his lucky shoes. Before the game, they
always warm up by stretching and jogging. It helps them

like “Great job!” or “Keep running!” to support them. The
referee watches closely. If someone breaks a rule, the
referee gives a yellow card.
Adam plays hard and always respects his team. He
drinks water, eats healthy food, and gets enough sleep.
He wants to stay fit and strong. After the match, they all
shake hands to show respect. Sometimes they play with
teams from other schools, so they learn to respect
different customs.
One Saturday, a team from another town visited. They
spoke a different language, so the players used hand
gestures and smiles to communicate. Adam gave a
thumbs-up when someone scored. Everyone had fun,
and they took a group photo at the end.
Moral:
 Playing sports is not just about winning. It’s about
teamwork, health, respect, and having fun together.

Youssef was selected to join his city’s youth football team
for an international tournament in Spain. It was the
biggest event of his life, and he was both excited and
nervous. The coach gave them a clear plan: train hard, stay
focused, and support one another on and off the field.

with a warm-up and light stretching to prevent injuries.
Then they practiced passing, dribbling, and team
strategies. Youssef wore a smartwatch to monitor his
heart rate and used a fitness app to record his progress.
“Train smart, not just hard,” the coach always said.
Before matches, the coach gave motivational talks.
“Communicate clearly,” he reminded them. “Use short
calls like ‘Man on!’ or ‘Switch!’ and respect the referee, no
matter what.”

teams didn’t speak English or Arabic. On the field, players
used simple gestures — a nod, a raised hand, a smile.
Before one match, the opposing team stood still during
the Jordanian national anthem. That small act of respect
meant a lot to Youssef.
During the semi-final, a player from the other team fell
and Youssef helped him up. After the game, the referee
praised both teams for their sportsmanship. Even though
Youssef’s team didn’t win the final, he felt proud.
He had improved his fitness, learned to work as part of a
team, and discovered that respect and fair play are more
powerful than winning.
Moral:
 Football is more than a game — it teaches discipline, unity,
and how to connect with others across cultures.
